extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of aesthetics, writers and critics interested in taste and the sublime/beautiful
extracted.subtask_description: A methodological and substantive framework for investigating the origins and qualities of the Sublime and the Beautiful in art and nature; includes how to conduct the inquiry and a long list of aesthetic dimensions (novelty, terror, obscurity, proportion, etc.) to consider when evaluating or producing works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious method of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceed with a cautious, 'timorous' method: avoid attempting to fly when you can scarcely creep; take small steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine complex matters gradually, do not overreach; prefer incremental argument and restrained claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine distinct ingredients one by one
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering any complex matter, examine every distinct ingredient in the composition separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce the subject to its simplest parts before recombining; avoid conflating multiple factors in a single move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce to utmost simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Simplify complex compositions to their simplest elements to reveal genuine principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simplification as a tool to make obscure or intricate phenomena intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative testing: re-examine principles and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: After analyzing parts, re-examine the principles by the effect of the composition and the composition by the principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iterative cross-checking between principles and their combined effects to validate theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparisons, including contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the subject with things of a similar nature and with things of a contrary nature; discoveries are often made by contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make many comparisons to improve generality and certainty of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large number of comparisons increases generality
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater the number of comparisons, the more general and certain the resulting knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately assemble varied examples to test whether proposed principles hold broadly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory founded on experiment/induction
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory should be founded on experiment (observable facts) rather than assumed axioms; it is valuable to the extent it explains phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical examples and observable effects as the basis of claims; inability to extend a theory indefinitely is not automatically fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address objections to principles or conclusions (not trivial examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections should be directed at the premises or the justness of conclusions, not offered as isolated poetic passages that don't bear on the principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid refutation-by-counterexample that targets peripheral instances; require objections to engage the structure of the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize clarity over elegance of style
rubrics_metrics.description: In difficult inquiries, submit style to matter and give up the praise of elegance when necessary to be clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor plain, clear exposition over literary polish if clarity requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope and state boundaries of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the limits of the inquiry (e.g., this work studies the origin of ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful, not a full dissertation on them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the project's scope early so readers judge conclusions fairly and avoid overstating claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit and incorporate criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek published criticisms and friends' candid remarks and use them to revise and improve the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterate drafts in light of reasoned objections and commentary before finalizing exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory need only explain what it covers
rubrics_metrics.description: A theory founded on facts is valuable in proportion to what it explains; inability to account for every image or passage doesn't overturn a general principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge theories by explanatory power over observed cases rather than by expectation of universal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and distinctness of classes (Sublime vs Beautiful)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities grouped under 'Sublime' should be consistent with one another and distinct from those grouped under 'Beauty'; names matter less than real differences in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing taxonomies, check internal coherence and inter-class opposition rather than rely solely on terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is treated as a factor relevant to the Sublime and Beautiful (chapter heading: 'Novelty').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how unexpectedness or newness contributes to aesthetic effect (no further detail in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pain and Pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation between pain and pleasure is a principal dimension to analyze in aesthetic response ('Pain and Pleasure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how sensations of pain and pleasure interact in producing aesthetic emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between removal of pain and positive pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish the relief from pain (removal) versus the direct presence of positive pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse whether an object's effect is the cessation of pain or an affirmative pleasurable feeling; the distinction matters for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delight versus Pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat delight and pleasure as opposing or differently-sourced experiences ('Of Delight and Pleasure, as opposed to each other').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discriminate finer shades of positive response—delight may differ in origin or quality from generic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joy and Grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish and analyze joy and grief as separate affective states relevant to taste and the Sublime/Beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how art elicits these opposing passions and the mechanisms behind them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passions belonging to self-preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and analyze the passions tied to self-preservation (e.g., fear, terror) as they relate to the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how threats or cues to self-preservation in a work trigger aesthetic responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the Sublime (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 'the Sublime' as a distinct class of qualities and passions, with its own causes and effects (chapter: 'Of the Sublime').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works for features that produce awe, terror, vastness, power, or other sublime effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passions belonging to society
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse passions that arise from social relations (honor, sympathy, ambition) and how they differ from self-preservation passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how social emotions shape aesthetic responses distinct from primal fears or pleasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cause of difference between self-preservation and social passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the ultimate reasons why passions tied to self-preservation differ from social passions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace functional or teleological explanations for divergence in affective reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 'Beauty' as a distinct class of qualities with its own consistent properties, different from the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate harmony, proportion, fitness, and pleasures of form when judging beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society and Solitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the effects of social context versus solitude on aesthetic responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how presence/absence of society modifies feelings like sympathy, imitation, or delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy, Imitation, and Ambition (cluster)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group sympathy, imitation, and ambition as interrelated mechanisms affecting taste and aesthetic response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine interactions among these three when analyzing character-driven or social aspects of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze sympathy as a distinct mechanism—how we feel for others' joys and sorrows—and its role in taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider extent, immediacy, and limits of sympathetic feeling when assessing emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of sympathy in the distresses of others
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how sympathy operates in response to others' distress and how that shapes the effect of tragic or moving works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether and how an artwork elicits vicarious suffering and moral sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of Tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the particular aesthetic effects produced by tragedy (how it moves, instructs, or purges passions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tragic works for mechanisms that produce pity, terror, or moral reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat imitation as an important aesthetic principle—how representation of actions/emotions produces response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fidelity, appropriateness, and the psychological effect of imitated actions or passions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze ambition as an aesthetic and social passion that influences character depiction and audience reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how ambition in characters or themes contributes to pathos, irony, or moral evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terror
rubrics_metrics.description: Terror is a key ingredient of the Sublime deserving separate analysis (Part II heading 'Terror').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine intensity, immediacy, and imagined danger that produce terror and thereby sublime impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Obscurity (lack of clearness) is examined as a factor in producing aesthetic passion and the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how vagueness, obscurity, or mysteriousness can heighten sublime feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness versus Obscurity with regard to the passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze how clearness and obscurity differently influence the passions and aesthetic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine when clarity aids emotional response and when obscurity augments it (e.g., by producing awe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power
rubrics_metrics.description: Power (magnitude of force or agency) is a component of the Sublime to be analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate representations of force, dominance, or overwhelming capability that create sublime impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privation
rubrics_metrics.description: Privation (absence, want) is treated as an aesthetic factor relevant to sublime or tragic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how lack or deprivation in a work contributes to poignancy or sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vastness
rubrics_metrics.description: Vastness (spatial or conceptual enormity) is a major cause of the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scale, extent, or immensity in works and their effect on awe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinity (or suggestion of limitless extent) is analyzed as producing sublime sensations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether elements of a work suggest boundlessness and how that affects feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession and Uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The temporal relations of succession and uniformity are considered as determinants of aesthetic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine patterns, rhythm, repetition, and their role in producing sublime or beautiful effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnitude in Building
rubrics_metrics.description: Magnitude as applied to architecture or constructed forms is treated as a specific source of the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess size, scale, and monumental qualities in built works when judging sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infinity in Pleasing Objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations of perceived infinity in objects that please (how limitlessness can be aesthetically pleasurable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how bordering-on-infinite qualities interact with delight or pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty (challenge or effort required) is treated as an aesthetic factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how perceived difficulty in production or comprehension contributes to admiration or sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnificence
rubrics_metrics.description: Magnificence (splendor, grand display) is considered a cause of aesthetic impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate splendour, ceremonial grandeur, and lavishness as means to impress or delight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light
rubrics_metrics.description: Light is analyzed for its aesthetic effects (Part II heading: 'Light').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how illumination, contrast, and chiaroscuro influence sublime or beautiful responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light in Building
rubrics_metrics.description: How light functions specifically in architectural contexts to produce aesthetic responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess distribution, scale, and framing of light in structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color considered as productive of the Sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Color is treated as a potential contributor to the Sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate color choices for their capacity to suggest vastness, terror, or other sublime qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound and Loudness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound, particularly loudness, is analyzed as an aesthetic cause (e.g., producing awe or alarm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess auditory intensity, timbre, and scale in relation to emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suddenness
rubrics_metrics.description: Suddenness (abrupt events) is examined as a trigger for strong aesthetic responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing and surprise for their role in producing terror or the sublime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermittence (on-and-off occurrences) is treated as an aesthetic factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rhythmic interruption and its impact on expectancy and emotional tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: The cries of animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal cries are analyzed as sources of aesthetic feeling (e.g., pathos, terror).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how natural sounds elicit sympathy, fear, or other passions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smell and Taste—Bitters and Stenches
rubrics_metrics.description: Olfactory and gustatory sensations (bitterness, stenches) are considered as contributors to aesthetic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how sensory disgust or pungency figures into aesthetic responses (rare but significant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeling—Pain
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical feeling and pain are analyzed with respect to their role in producing aesthetic emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the boundary between physical sensation and its imaginative/aesthetic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the cause of Beauty in vegetables
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that proportion alone does not explain beauty in plants (Part III heading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning causes of beauty, test proportional explanations against counterexamples in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the cause of Beauty in animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that proportion alone does not account for animal beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine alternative causes (color, motion, expression) beyond mere proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion not the cause of Beauty in the human species
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that proportion is not the sole determinant of human beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider expression, sympathy, and other qualities alongside proportion when judging human beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion further considered
rubrics_metrics.description: A deeper examination of proportion and its limits as an explanation for beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept proportion as a comprehensive account without further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness not the cause of Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Fitness (suitability or appropriateness) is argued not to be the fundamental cause of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate practical fitness from aesthetic appeal when analyzing beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: The real effects of Fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider what fitness does produce (its real effects) as distinct from being the cause of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse downstream effects of perceived fitness on pleasure or judgment without conflating cause and consequence.
